tomato_early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown concentric rings (target spot pattern) surrounded by a yellow halo on lower mature leaves.

organic_measures.name: Copper Hydroxide / Bordeaux Mixture Spray
organic_measures.method: Apply copper-based organic fungicide (1-2 g per liter) thoroughly on both leaf surfaces.
organic_measures.application: Foliar spray during cool morning or evening hours
organic_measures.frequency: Every 7 to 10 days until disease progression halts

organic_measures.name: Bio-fungicide (Trichoderma viride / Bacillus subtilis)
organic_measures.method: Spray Trichoderma viride or Bacillus subtilis formulation (5 g/ml per liter of water) to outcompete fungal spores.

chemical_measures.name: Mancozeb 75% WP
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Wear PPE (gloves, mask, goggles). Do not spray during bloom period. Pre-harvest interval (PHI): 7 days.

prevention_measures: Practice 2-3 year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
Use drip irrigation instead of overhead watering to keep foliage dry.
Apply organic straw or plastic mulch around the plant base to prevent soil-splash.
sources: ICAR - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR) Tomato Disease Guide
University of Florida IFAS Extension: Early Blight of Tomato
FAO Integrated Pest Management in Vegetable Production

tomato_late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions on leaves and stems with white cottony fungal growth on leaf undersides in humid conditions.

organic_measures.name: Copper Oxychloride Spray
organic_measures.method: Spray copper oxychloride (2.5 g/L) immediately upon first symptom detection.
organic_measures.frequency: Every 5 to 7 days in high humidity

chemical_measures.name: Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Wear protective gear. Observe 14-day pre-harvest interval.

prevention_measures: Destroy infected plant debris immediately; do not compost.
Maintain wide plant spacing for enhanced air circulation.
Plant resistant cultivars where available.
sources: UC Davis IPM: Tomato Late Blight Management

tomato_bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked leaf spots that become angular with yellow borders; raised scabby spots on fruit.

organic_measures.name: Fixed Copper + Mancozeb Mix (Organic/Biorational)
organic_measures.method: Apply copper hydroxide formulation (2 g/L) combined with neem oil emulsion.

chemical_measures.name: Streptomycin Sulphate + Tetracycline Hydrochloride
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Use strictly according to local antibiotic regulation limits in agriculture.

prevention_measures: Use certified pathogen-free seeds and transplants.
Avoid handling plants when foliage is wet.
Sanitize tools and stakes with 10% bleach solution.
sources: Cornell Cooperative Extension Tomato Bacterial Spot Sheet

tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small circular spots with grayish-white centers and dark brown margins containing tiny black fruiting bodies.

organic_measures.name: Potassium Bicarbonate / Copper Spray
organic_measures.method: Spray potassium bicarbonate (3-4 g/L) or copper hydroxide (2 g/L).

chemical_measures.name: Chlorothalonil 75% WP
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Avoid inhalation and eye contact. Wear goggles and respirator.

prevention_measures: Remove and prune lower leaves up to 12 inches from the soil surface.
Rotate crops out of Solanaceae family for 2 years.
Mulch heavily around base.
sources: Purdue University Extension: Septoria Leaf Spot of Tomato

tomato_leaf_mold.symptoms: Pale green to yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces with velvety olive-green to brown fungal growth underneath.

organic_measures.name: Bio-fungicide & Humidity Control
organic_measures.method: Spray Bacillus subtilis (5 ml/L). Increase greenhouse ventilation to lower relative humidity below 85%.

chemical_measures.name: Difenoconazole 25% EC
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Do not enter sprayed area for 24 hours without PPE.

prevention_measures: Ensure high air exchange in protected green houses.
Space plants adequately.
Avoid overhead irrigation.
sources: University of Minnesota Extension: Leaf Mold of Tomato

tomato_spider_mites.symptoms: Yellow stippling/speckling on leaves, fine silky webbing on undersides, leaf yellowing and bronze drying.

organic_measures.name: Neem Oil 10,000 ppm / Insecticidal Soap
organic_measures.method: Spray cold-pressed neem oil (5 ml/L) mixed with mild liquid soap, thoroughly covering leaf undersides.

chemical_measures.name: Abamectin 1.9% EC
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Highly toxic to bees; apply strictly during non-blooming periods or evening.

prevention_measures: Maintain adequate humidity and avoid drought stress.
Introduce predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis) in protected structures.
Keep field borders clear of dusty weeds.
sources: UC Davis IPM: Two-spotted Spider Mite on Tomato

tomato_target_spot.symptoms: Pinpoint brown spots expanding into circular lesions with light brown centers and dark brown margins.

organic_measures.name: Copper Octanoate / Bordeaux Spray
organic_measures.method: Spray organic copper octanoate formulation (2-3 ml/L).

chemical_measures.name: Azoxystrobin 23% SC
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Alternate with different fungicide classes to avoid resistance buildup.

prevention_measures: Improve canopy aeration by staking and suckering.
Avoid planting near alternate host crops.
sources: UF/IFAS Extension Target Spot Management Guide

tomato_yellow_leaf_curl_virus.symptoms: Severe leaf curling (upward/inward), yellowing margins, stunted bushy growth, flower abortion.

organic_measures.name: Whitefly Vector Management (Neem + Yellow Sticky Traps)
organic_measures.method: Install 15-20 yellow sticky traps per acre. Spray neem oil (5 ml/L) or Beauveria bassiana (5 g/L) to control whiteflies.
organic_measures.frequency: Continuous trap monitoring; spray every 5-7 days

chemical_measures.name: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (Vector Control)
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Harmful to pollinators. Do not apply during flowering.

prevention_measures: Use TYLCV-resistant hybrids.
Use 50-mesh insect-proof netting over nurseries.
Rogue out infected plants early.
sources: ICAR-IIHR Tomato Virus Disease Control Protocol

tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Light and dark green mottling/mosaic pattern on leaves, leaf distortion, fern-like stringy leaf blading.

organic_measures.name: Sanitation & Milk Spray Washing
organic_measures.method: Wash hands/tools in skim milk (20% solution) or trisodium phosphate before touching plants to deactivate viral particles.

prevention_measures: No chemical cure exists for viral infections; prevention is paramount.
Use virus-free certified seeds.
Prohibit tobacco use near tomato fields due to cross-contamination risk.
sources: APS Plant Disease Lessons: Tomato Mosaic Virus

tomato_healthy.symptoms: Vibrant green foliage, sturdy stems, uniform growth with no signs of spots, curling, or discoloration.

organic_measures.name: Routine Crop Nutrition & Bio-stimulant
organic_measures.method: Apply liquid seaweed extract or compost tea (5 ml/L) as a foliar tonic to maintain robust immunity.

prevention_measures: Maintain balanced N-P-K fertilization and micro-nutrients (Calcium, Magnesium).
Monitor soil moisture consistently.
Inspect weekly for early pest/disease incursions.
sources: ICAR Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) for Solanaceous Crops
